title: inspection-findings
description: The envelope one inspection of one scope writes. It is a file the agent wrote rather than anything parsed out of what it printed: a format enforced by nothing breaks silently, and a malformed finding read out of prose would be indistinguishable from no finding at all. THE ENVELOPE HOLDS `findings` TO BEING A REQUIRED ARRAY AND TO NOTHING MORE, and that is deliberate rather than lax. This validator subset has no reference keyword, so restating the brief's fields here would be a second definition of a shape this repository defines once in schemas/story-brief.schema.json — two definitions that agree today and drift the first time either is edited. Each entry is instead judged one at a time by the reader: the loop in orchestration/inspection.py that judges findings holds each finding to the brief schema on its own, and the filter beside it judges each area suggestion on its own. That is what makes a refused entry of either kind cost only itself: it is dropped and named — with the field that failed, or with what was wrong with it — and the entries beside it in the same file are filed or reported exactly as they would have been. An envelope with `findings` absent or not an array is still refused as a whole, because there is nothing in it to judge one at a time.

findings.description: The findings this inspection of this scope produced. The envelope holds this to being an array and nothing more: each entry is judged one at a time by the loop in orchestration/inspection.py that reads it, which holds each finding to schemas/story-brief.schema.json on its own, so a finding that fails that schema — and a finding that is not an object at all, a string or a null — is dropped and named by its position or its slug, and the findings beside it are filed exactly as they would have been. An empty array is an answer rather than an absence: it says the Inspector looked at this scope and found nothing worth filing.

area_suggestions.description: What the Inspector could name no area for, and what it thinks each such brief concerns. Optional: an envelope carrying only `findings` is what every inspection wrote before this existed and is what an inspection of a target declaring no area vocabulary goes on writing. THE SHAPE IT EXPECTS IS A LIST OF ENTRIES, each an object carrying a `slug` string — the slug of the finding this suggestion is about, spelled exactly as that finding spells it, which is how a report matches a suggestion to a brief that was actually filed — and a `concerns` string, what that brief seems to concern in the Inspector's own words, so a person can decide whether the target's vocabulary is missing a line. THE ENVELOPE HOLDS THE FIELD TO NONE OF THAT, and that is deliberate rather than lax: each entry is judged one at a time by the reader rather than by the envelope, because IT IS READ FOR THE REPORT AND FILED BY NOTHING — a suggestion never reaches a brief, a payload, an outbox entry or a tracker, since the vocabulary grows by a person editing the target's own document and a name no developer has approved must not be filed under — so a field reaching nothing may not become the thing that stops an inspection. An entry that is not a usable pair — not an object, `slug` or `concerns` missing or not a string, or blank — is dropped and named, by its slug where it carries a readable one and otherwise by its position, with what was wrong with it, in the same list where the inspection reports its other drops; a field that is not a list at all is dropped and named as one such entry. Refused entries cost the entries beside them nothing: those are reported exactly as they would have been. That is exactly how a malformed finding is treated. A refused entry still counts, as a usable one does, as evidence that the target declares an area vocabulary, so the briefs beside it that named no area are still reported as area-less. `orchestration/inspection.py`'s `_area_suggestions` is the filter that judges each entry. What the field buys is that a missing area is reported rather than silent, which is the whole reason naming none is a first-class answer.
